query:
While Jerome was walking Cecilia through a PixInsight Ha-RGB blending workflow, someone in the chat acknowledged following the walkthrough closely but explicitly positioned themselves as outside the narrowband-PixInsight process. Who was that person?

Options:
A. Dev
B. Ruth
C. Marcus
D. Tomás
context:
[1] (about=Dev, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:41:00) is that a dumb question but... if I wanted to learn PixInsight where would I even start? lowkey the walkthrough Jerome just did made more sense to me than any YouTube video I've tried
[2] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:11:00) that is exactly what the Ha-RGB blend does. you keep the full broadband RGB as your colour base and add the Ha emission only where it contributes signal. the PixInsight workflow I use is: LinearFit both datasets to match background levels, then use PixelMath with the expression: Ha_weight multiplied by Ha plus open-bracket 1 minus Ha_weight close-bracket multiplied by R, where Ha_weight is typically 0.7. you replace the red channel with this blended value and recombine. the result is your broadband warmth with Ha emission boosting the ionised hydrogen regions. it is the best of both methods technically speaking. try it on the Orion core and tell me if the Trapezium halo structure changes.
[3] (about=Cecilia, said_by=Jerome, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:04:00) Jerome says the issue with Cecilia's Ha channel is almost certainly her background extraction in PixInsight; if she uses automatic background extractor before separating channels, she will get a muddy look. He will walk her through the correct sequence in 20 minutes.
[4] (about=Jerome, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:22:00) send me the FITS file. the issue is almost certainly your background extraction in PixInsight. if you are using automatic background extractor before separating the channels you will get that muddy look. I will walk you through the correct sequence. it will take 20 minutes.
[5] (about=Harriet, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:39:00) I am going to put this whole thread in the podcast episode notes. Jerome, you are better at teaching than you think you are.
